title: The Legend of the Demon King of Nanatsureki Island: Murder Case File Zweite
paragraphs: “Ha ha! Alright! Let the paradise begin!”

And just like that, the ugly orgy of carnal desire—led by Takt and his pack of pigs—began. Of course, depending on his mood, Takt would start getting it on with the pigs right in broad daylight. He’s the very embodiment of lust.

It’s kind of gross, like I’m looking at my past self, but even I never went that far without any self-restraint. That’s right… Takt’s orgy with the pigs somehow overlaps with that of the Pig King. I believe they were distant relatives.

According to Rival, she was a “trophy wife,” wasn’t she? That’s how he treats those pigs. I don’t sense any obsession or genuine love for them. From a man’s perspective, it feels like he just cares about his own pleasure.
Well, never mind… Takt and the others probably haven’t the faintest idea that the feast about to begin is a terrifying one. After all, my goal is to see their faces contort with fear!

By the way, I’ve heard this island is protected by a magical barrier cast by dragons, griffins, and foxes, cutting it off completely from the outside world. And… in the distant sky, the storm created by Rival with magic is gradually gaining strength and drawing closer.
“Oink! Oink-oink!”

Oh? In the island’s botanical garden… there’s the pig and the piglet who deceived Mistira. Heh heh heh, I haven’t forgotten my comrade Mistira. I’ll let her witness me brutally disposing of this pig once again. By doing so, Mistira will be able to move forward. “Revenge begets revenge”… well, I couldn’t care less about that. It’s a good thing, since the scourge of this world will be wiped from the face of the earth.
“O-o-oink!”

And so the feast began… a hideous orgy of carnal desire between Takt and the pig, taking place right in broad daylight. Eventually… it was nightfall, and the storm summoned by Rival had engulfed the island. On Seven Island, where the storm raged, in one of the mansions Takt had built, the dragon possessed by the Rival slowly sauntered in, accompanied by a fox, a griffin, and four others.
“Raildia, I hear you’re holding a secret gathering for Takt—what’s this all about?”
“Exactly. Let’s at least hear what he’s thinking.”
“Oink.”
“Bubhee”
“Booh”
“Boo-boo”
Oh? Looks like the pig who used to be the representative of Shieldfreeden is mixed in here too. That Rival of mine has gathered quite the fine group.
“More importantly, I didn’t hear anything about a storm like this coming.”
“The wind’s imbued with Magical Power, and I suppose the barrier is acting strangely.”
“Enough already, Raildia. You’re the one who’s going to clear this storm!”
The fox and the griffin are saying something without seeming the least bit suspicious. The storm was created by our Rival, you know.
“Hold on a moment—this is also an event I devised.”
“Huh… What’s that muscle-headed Dragon Emperor up to?”
“Let’s at least hear him out. It’s probably just some nonsense anyway, right? I’ll make sure to tell Takt about it.”
“Boo-boo!”
“Oink!”
And so, tilting their heads slightly, the pigs wait for the dragon—possessed by their Rival—to answer.
“Do you lot know the legend of this island?”
That’s the one we heard in the last loop. Something about a Demon King split into seven pieces or something like that.
“Ah, that legend.”
“That’s the villain from way back when who said he’d turn the tables on Takt if he showed up, right?”
“Oink, oink.”
“Oink?”
Well then, it’s time to spill the beans.
“Ah, actually… that’s it!”
“That’s it?”
“Oink-hyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!”
The screams of the maid pigs echo through the mansion Takt has prepared.
“W-what’s going on!?”

Takt heard the pig’s scream and rushed over. Of course, the other pigs came running one after another as well. There are so many of them living in this mansion that you’d wonder, “Just how many are there?” I’m really looking forward to the slaughter.
“O-o-ooh…”
Trembling uncontrollably, the maid pig points toward a private room. And there, inside…
“Tu, Tulina!? W-what on earth is going on!?”
Takt entered the room and shouted as he examined the corpse of the fox—which had returned to its true form after its head had been blown off.
“O-oink…”
“Oi-i-iink!?”

Seeing the fox’s corpse, the pigs all reacted in their own ways. But I can tell. They were all just pigs secretly smiling so Takt wouldn’t see. They probably just think that a nuisance has met a gruesome end.
“Tulina! Hey! Pull yourself together! That’s it! As long as her soul is still there, we should be able to revive her with a homunculus, right!?”
“O-oink!”

The pig in the white coat looks around with what appears to be a telescope. He’s shaking his head vigorously. He’s probably saying he can’t find the fox’s soul anywhere nearby. Even I can figure that much out.
HAHAHA! There’s no way it’s here. After all, I took care of it—soul and all! And even if it really had been here, didn’t you pigs say there wasn’t one to begin with?
“Who on earth pulled a stunt like this?!”
Oh? Takt’s eyes are filled with rage, yet his reaction is surprisingly calm. Ah, I see. That’s because there’s supposed to be nothing but trophy pigs on the island.
“Bubub…”

It seems the maid pig explained the situation to Takt. Well, I was watching from hiding, so I kind of figured it out. The maid pig found the local symbol drawn on the door suspicious, so she opened it with the master key she’d been given—pretending she was just cleaning the room. And that’s when she discovered the corpse.
“…Is there something clutched in Tulina’s hand? What is this…!?”

Saying this, Takt found the key clutched in the fox’s paw and checked the room number. Swallowing hard, Takt and the others headed to the room corresponding to the key the fox had been holding and checked inside. And there, they found…
“No way… Ashil…!?”
Takt was left speechless once again. Lying there inside the room was the lifeless body of Griffin, his right arm missing!
“Ashilrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrr!”

Takt let out a bloodcurdling scream and began crying dramatically. HAHAHA! But that’s nothing compared to the suffering of Filolial-sama, whom you killed! Suddenly, Takt stopped crying and began examining Griffin’s corpse more closely. He sure switches gears quickly.
“This is… could it be…?”

Of course, in Takt’s hand was yet another room key. And so, one by one, Takt and his pig companions used the keys to open the rooms. The corpse of the dragon that Rival had possessed was also lying in one of the rooms.
“This… something… crawled out of its belly…?”
The dragon’s corpse, which Rival had possessed, had died with a hole in its abdomen. That hole led to a passage in the wall just big enough for a mouse to squeeze through.
“Ooogggg!”
“Ooogggggaaaaaaah!”
The pigs are squealing “Oink, oink,” but Takt murmurs to himself, blinking a few times.
“Reldia’s corpse had its stomach ripped open… Is this the one who killed everyone else…?”
“Oink! Oink, oink!”
And there goes the pig in the white coat, squawking away. I can’t make head or tail of what it’s saying.
“A ritual to revive the Seven-Split Demon King!? That’s ridiculous… but… all the places where everyone was torn apart, just as the legend described, are gone…”
Takt muttered this while looking at the corpses of the dead pigs, letting out a dry, hollow laugh. At that very moment, a pig came running up.
“Oink-oink!?”
“Oink!?”
“Huh!? The ship, the submarine, the airplane—even the manufacturing dock—they’ve all been destroyed, leaving not a trace!?”
To confirm this, Takt took the pigs with him and checked every location where the vehicles had been.
“Oink-oink-oink!”
“Oink!”
“Oink-oink!”
Realizing there was no way to leave the island, the pigs started squabbling among themselves. Pigs really are a vile lot who put their own lives first, aren’t they?
“Hold on, hold on. There’s no way we can leave the island in this storm. We can’t even use our teleportation Skills because of the barrier Raildia and the others set up.”
“Boo-boo!”
Takt, cornered by the pigs, yelled at them with an exasperated look on his face.
“Just calm down, will you! All of you!”
The strong wind and rain were lashing against the windows of the mansion.
“Hmph. With everyone’s Magic, we should be able to blow this weather away! Then we can set sail gracefully on calm seas!”
Well, it seems they’re acting all nonchalant and making plans to blow the storm away. Takt seems to be leading the pigs in chanting Ceremonial Magic to try and dispel the storm.
“Ceremonial Magic!”

Just as Takt was casting the spell… I nullified it with Absorb. I completely wiped out that spell meant to blow away the oncoming storm! HAHAHA. Even if they did blow it away, the storm would just regenerate immediately! I hear that’s exactly how Rival keeps using magic.
“H-hey… what the hell is this?!”
Takt looked up at the stormy sky, clearly annoyed that things weren’t going his way. No matter how many pigs gather, it’s such shoddy magic that it has absolutely no effect!
“Oink oink oink!”
As if to say, “Looks like you’re in a pickle,” the Shark Pig spoke to Takt.
“Wait… that’s it! You could swim your way out of this storm, couldn’t you?”
“Oink oink!”
The Shark Pig nodded. ……Are you really sure that’s a good idea? A single choice can sometimes lead to disaster, you know?
“Then let’s get going right away! Take me with you and get off the island! I’ll arrange for a large plane to come pick everyone up later.”
“Oink-oink!”
“Oink!”
“Oink-oink!”
The pigs began swarming around Shark Pig and Takt.

“Oh, for heaven’s sake! You lot! You know this is an emergency, right? Fine… You know we’re the strongest in the world, don’t you? Shate, you get out of here and arrange for a plane—I’ll take down the imposter posing as the Demon King.”
“Oink!”
With that, Shark Pig leaped into the sea, signaling he understood. Using it as a marker, Shark Pig made his ring glow with Magic as he swam off.
“Everyone! We can breathe a little easier now. I think we can win if we fight, but we don’t know what might happen. Let’s stick together and act as one.”
“Oink-oink!”
“Oink!”
“The Demon King doesn’t scare us! Got it? In a situation like this, barricading ourselves in is the dumbest thing we could do!　We just need to stick together and find a way off the island.”

Those filthy pigs were clinging to the Shark Pig without batting an eye, desperate to escape the island, but since they didn’t want to get dirty, they seemed to accept Takt’s suggestion and quietly prioritized their own safety.
“Anyway, everyone, stick together… We’re going to search every corner of this island and make the culprit pay with their blood!”
Still calm—or rather, burning with a thirst for revenge—Takt seemed intent on identifying the culprit lurking on the island. As for what I was doing at that moment…
“Bwah—!?”

I approached the Shark Pig, which had dived into the sea, in Submarine Mode, finished it off with a single thrust, and then headed straight out to sea with it. Did it really think it could escape? Too bad. I won’t let you escape this island.

Of course, not only did it die instantly, but I’ve already disposed of its soul as well. I tossed it out so the ocean currents would wash it ashore. With the cover of night, it’ll be quite difficult to find, I imagine.
Anyway, Takt and his pig cronies were combing the entire island thoroughly in the middle of the night. But there’s no way the likes of you could ever find me!
A few hours later. I discarded a couple of pigs—the ones who showed a moment of weakness—right in front of the shrine on the island Rival had specified.
“Ooogggghh!?”
The pigs who found the corpses called out to Takt and the others.
“A priest who spoke of stopping the Demon King’s resurrection was brutally murdered… Don’t mess with me! I know this is a staged murder!”

Takt started shooting the pigs glances laced with a hint of murderous intent. He must think the culprit is among them. With so many suspects, do you really think you can pinpoint the one with your own brain?
“Oink!”
“Oink-oink!”

It looks like the pigs are about to get into an argument with Takt just to save their own skins. Haha! Keep fighting! After all, that’s how shallow the relationship is between you pigs and Takt. You’re literally just trophy pigs! Takt!
“Oink! Oink!”
The maid pig stepped in to try and calm things down.
“E-Ellie… You’re right. If we fight here, we’ll be playing right into the culprit’s hands.”
“Oink…”
“Tch!”

There’s even a pig among them who’s clicking their tongue. Tch… that maid pig. Seems she’s got more brains than she needs. So, the pigs took refuge inside the mansion. The mansion Takt had prepared was fairly spacious and divided into separate sections.
Now then… in time with the resurrection ritual and following Rival’s instructions… I let a deafening explosion ring out.
“W-what!?”
“Ooogggh!?”

I unleashed “Liberation Prominence” right at the building at the end of the connecting corridor in the section of the mansion where the pigs had taken refuge. By the way, this section is where the pigs who had grown tiresome to Takt were discreetly assigned. According to Rival, ever since I saved them around Volume 2, they’ve been nothing but dead weight or something like that. In short, they’re the kind of folks you couldn’t care less about. The building was blown to smithereens by my Magic.
“The Demon King has descended to demonstrate his power…”
Takt held his breath, put out the fire from the vanished building, and then muttered to himself as he inspected the scene.
“What do you mean, ‘demonstrate his power’! You used the explosives I developed, didn’t you! Don’t mess with me!”
Oh? Do you really think a pathetic little invention like yours could produce this much firepower? Panda defused it in a flash! HAHAHA!
“I’m checking our explosives inventory! And maintaining the defensive barrier while I’m at it!”
It looks like Takt has gone on the defensive. He’s also set up tight security.
Additionally, files 1 and 3 do not exist.
